domains_and_motifs.name: Nuclear localization signal (N-terminal)
domains_and_motifs.description: N-terminal nuclear location signal with conserved pattern (Pro, followed by Lys or Arg in 3 out of 5 residues)

sources.notes: Monopartite NLS in conserved nuclear receptor binding domain

domains_and_motifs.name: TAZ1 domain (CH1)
domains_and_motifs.description: Transcriptional adapter zinc finger domain 1 (TAZ1), also called CH1. Four-helix bundle zinc finger that binds intrinsically disordered transactivation domains of multiple transcription factors including HIF-1A, CITED2, STAT2, p53, and others. Critical for hypoxia response and transcriptional regulation.

sources.notes: Four-helix bundle structure determined by NMR

domains_and_motifs.name: KIX domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Kinase-inducible domain interacting (KIX) domain. CREB binding domain that specifically recognizes phosphorylated CREB (pSer133) and other transcription factors including c-Myb. Three-helix bundle with two-helix coiled-coil.

domains_and_motifs.name: Bromodomain
domains_and_motifs.description: Bromodomain that recognizes and binds acetylated lysine residues on histones (acetyl-lysine reader). Critical for maintaining histone acetyltransferase signaling and chromatin localization. Four-helix bundle structure with acetyl-lysine binding pocket.

domains_and_motifs.name: PHD finger
domains_and_motifs.description: Plant homeodomain (PHD) finger. Cys4-His-Cys3 zinc finger motif forming cross-brace topology with two zinc atoms. May recognize histone methylation marks.

domains_and_motifs.name: RING domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Atypical RING-type zinc finger domain unique to CBP/p300. May be involved in E3 ubiquitin ligase activity in cytoplasmic compartment.

domains_and_motifs.name: Histone acetyltransferase (HAT) domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Catalytic histone acetyltransferase domain (KAT3A activity). Transfers acetyl groups from acetyl-CoA to lysine residues on histones H2B (K13), H3 (K15, K18, K27) and H4 (K9). Also acetylates non-histone proteins. Can also use other acyl-CoA substrates for propionylation and lactylation.

domains_and_motifs.name: Nuclear localization signal (bipartite)
domains_and_motifs.description: Central bipartite nuclear localization signal, highly conserved in mouse CREBBP and in p300

domains_and_motifs.name: ZZ-type zinc finger
domains_and_motifs.description: ZZ-type zinc finger domain. Contains two twisted antiparallel beta-sheets and short alpha-helix. Binds two zinc ions via CXXC and HXH motifs. Cross-brace zinc finger fold related to PHD and RING domains.

sources.notes: Unusual zinc coordination with CXXC and HXH motifs

domains_and_motifs.name: TAZ2 domain (CH3)
domains_and_motifs.description: Transcriptional adapter zinc finger domain 2 (TAZ2), also called CH3. Four-helix bundle that binds transactivation domains of STAT1, p53, and other transcription factors. Contains both ZZ and TAZ2 zinc-binding motifs. Preferentially binds smaller TADs restricted to single contiguous binding surface.

sources.notes: Solution structure determined; residues Pro1727-Gln1747 (alpha1), Pro1756-Lys1769 (alpha2), Pro1780-His1795 (alpha3), Pro1804-Lys1810 (alpha4)

domains_and_motifs.name: CREB binding domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Additional CREB interaction region distinct from KIX domain

alphafold_prediction.confidence_summary: Global pLDDT score 52.52 indicates moderate overall confidence. Structured domains (TAZ1, KIX, bromodomain, HAT) show high confidence (pLDDT >70). Low confidence regions (pLDDT <50) likely correspond to intrinsically disordered linkers and glutamine-rich regions, which are expected to be unstructured in isolation.

post_translational_modifications.function: Regulates p300/CREBBP nucleocytoplasmic shuttling in response to amino acid/glucose depletion. AMP-activated protein kinase-dependent phosphorylation causes cytoplasm-to-nucleus relocalization.
CREBBP can autoacetylate; acetylation may regulate HAT activity and protein-protein interactions
Subject to ubiquitin-mediated regulation; CBP/p300 also possess E4 ubiquitin ligase activity in cytoplasm

function.uniprot_function: Acetylates histones, giving a specific tag for transcriptional activation. Acts as a scaffold to stabilize additional protein interactions with the transcription complex. Mediates cAMP-gene regulation by binding specifically to phosphorylated CREB protein. Functions as a transcriptional coactivator for numerous transcription factors including AP-1, MyoD, MEF-2, nuclear receptors, CREB, HIF-1alpha, p53, STAT proteins, beta-catenin, and many others. Has intrinsic histone acetyltransferase activity; acetylates both histone and non-histone proteins. Acetylates histone H3 at 'Lys-18' (H3K18ac) and 'Lys-27' (H3K27ac), as well as histone H2B at 'Lys-13', H3 at 'Lys-15', and H4 at 'Lys-9'. Also acetylates non-histone proteins including DDX21, FBL, IRF2, MAFG, NCOA3, POLR1E/PAF53, FOXO1, and p53. Plays essential role in embryonic development, cell growth, transformation, and regulation of circadian rhythm.
function.catalytic_activity: Acetyl-CoA + [histone]-L-lysine = CoA + [histone]-N6-acetyl-L-lysine. Can also use propionyl-CoA and lactoyl-CoA as substrates for histone propionylation and lactylation, respectively.
function.tissue_specificity: Ubiquitously expressed with low tissue specificity (Tau score 0.27). Expressed in all examined tissues as a fundamental transcriptional coactivator.

molecular_function.term: DNA-binding transcription factor activity, RNA polymerase II-specific

reactome.pathway_name: CREB phosphorylation through the activation of CaMKII

pathways.pathway_role_summary: CREBBP functions as a master transcriptional coactivator integrating signals from multiple pathways including cAMP/PKA (CREB), hypoxia (HIF-1A), Wnt (beta-catenin), p53 stress response, interferon signaling (STATs), and Notch. Acts as a molecular scaffold and chromatin modifier, using its HAT activity to acetylate histones and non-histone proteins, thereby regulating gene expression in development, metabolism, circadian rhythm, and stress responses.

disease_associations.description: Autosomal dominant developmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, broad thumbs and halluces, short stature, and facial dysmorphisms. Caused by CREBBP haploinsufficiency due to mutations, deletions, or chromosomal rearrangements. About 60% of RSTS cases are due to CREBBP mutations (vs 8% from EP300). Over 246 disease-causing mutations reported including point mutations, small indels, translocations, inversions, and large deletions.

Patients with RSTS have increased risk of tumors including meningioma, pilomatrixoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, pheochromocytoma, neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, and leukemia. CREBBP acts as tumor suppressor; germline loss-of-function increases cancer susceptibility.

Somatic CREBBP mutations are frequent in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), follicular lymphoma, and other B-cell malignancies. Mutations often affect HAT domain, creating 'zombie enzymes' with altered chromatin loading that prevent EP300 compensation. CREBBP and EP300 show synthetic lethality in DLBCL.

CREBBP alterations including chromosomal translocations and somatic mutations occur in multiple solid tumors including melanomas, gastric, colorectal, and squamous cell carcinomas. Both loss-of-function (tumor suppressor) and overexpression (oncogenic) contexts observed.

metadata.data_quality_notes: High-quality data available for structured domains (TAZ1, TAZ2, KIX, bromodomain, HAT) with multiple crystal structures and NMR structures. Many quantitative binding affinities available for key transcription factor interactions (p53, HIF-1A, CITED2, STATs, CREB). AlphaFold prediction shows moderate confidence (pLDDT 52.52) due to extensive intrinsically disordered regions and low-complexity glutamine-rich sequences, which are expected. Some interaction partners lack quantitative kinetic data (CTNNB1, KMT2A, CDKN1A). PTM sites from PhosphoSitePlus not fully enumerated; focused on functionally characterized modifications.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: CREBBP is a master transcriptional coactivator and chromatin modifier critical for integrating multiple signaling pathways. Key for modeling: (1) Multi-domain scaffold protein with well-characterized binding affinities for numerous transcription factors, enabling quantitative modeling of competitive binding; (2) HAT enzymatic activity with measured kinetic parameters for histone acetylation; (3) Nucleocytoplasmic shuttling regulated by nutrient/energy status provides spatial regulation; (4) Dual function as nuclear transcriptional activator (acetylation) and cytoplasmic E4 ubiquitin ligase (degradation) enables context-dependent regulation; (5) Central node in Wnt, p53, hypoxia, cAMP, and interferon signaling pathways. High-quality structural and kinetic data make CREBBP suitable for mechanistic rule-based modeling of signal integration and transcriptional regulation.
